title: Works on the Server, Refused From Everywhere Else
intro: A new Redis cache was installed on cache-01. The developer says 'it works fine, I tested it' — but every app server gets 'connection refused'.

steps.prompt: From an app server, test the Redis port on cache-01.
steps.fake_output: nc: connect to cache-01 port 6379 (tcp) failed: Connection refused
steps.hint: Refused, not timed out — what does that tell you about the network path?

steps.prompt: Refused means the host answered. On cache-01, check which address Redis is listening on.
It's bound to 127.0.0.1 — reachable only from cache-01 itself. That's why the developer's local test passed. Find the bind setting in the config.
After changing bind to the private interface IP (10.0.4.40) and enabling requirepass, restart Redis.
steps.hint: Config changes only apply after a restart.
Same test as the first step.

resolution: Redis (like Postgres, MySQL, and many others) binds to 127.0.0.1 by default precisely so a fresh install isn't exposed to the network. The developer's test ran ON cache-01, where localhost works — the classic 'works on my machine' at the network layer. 'Connection refused' was the key clue: the host was reachable, it just had nothing listening on the external interface. The fix binds to the specific private IP rather than 0.0.0.0, and requires a password — Redis exposed on 0.0.0.0 without auth is one of the most commonly exploited misconfigurations on the internet. Pair it with a firewall rule allowing 6379 only from the app servers' subnet.
